--- title: "Most draft-eligible college seasons end without an NFL outcome" date: "2026-10-24" description: "Only 3.6% of draft-eligible college player-seasons end in a draft selection and 8.3% in NFL entry, more entrants arrive undrafted than drafted, the per-season entry chance rises from 4.1% to 20.4% by the fourth eligible season, and the drafted share fell from 5.9% (2012 class) to 2.6% (2025)." followups: - "Evaluate out-of-time models with calibration metrics, since the positive class is rarer in later draft classes than in training data." - "Include the eligible-season index as a model term; the entry hazard varies fourfold across it." - "Treat made-roster and rookie-games as a separate second-stage prediction problem, not a footnote on entry." author: - "AI directed by Nick Giangreco" freeze: auto vignette: > %\VignetteIndexEntry{Most draft-eligible college seasons end without an NFL outcome} %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html} %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8} --- ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ---- Packages, data connection and figure defaults ------------------------- # Load the project's functions straight from the checkout with pkgload; the # repo is never installed (decision 0042). The site build sets CFB2NFL_ROOT, # a local render finds the checkout from the working directory. root <- Sys.getenv("CFB2NFL_ROOT") if (!nzchar(root)) root <- pkgload::pkg_path() knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root) pkgload::load_all(root, quiet = TRUE) con <- DBI::dbConnect( duckdb::duckdb(), file.path(root, "data", "cfb2nfl.duckdb"), read_only = TRUE ) library(DBI) library(dplyr) library(duckdb) library(ggiraph) library(ggplot2) library(knitr) library(tibble) library(tidyr) set_girafe_defaults( opts_hover = opts_hover( css = "stroke:#111827;stroke-width:2.5px;filter:brightness(1.12);" ), opts_hover_inv = opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.45;"), opts_tooltip = opts_tooltip( css = "background:#111827;color:#fff;padding:6px 9px;border-radius:5px;font-weight:bold;font-size:15px;" ), opts_zoom = opts_zoom(min = 1, max = 5), opts_toolbar = opts_toolbar(saveaspng = TRUE, position = "topright"), opts_sizing = opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE) ) # Wilson interval for a binomial proportion. wilson <- function(x, n, z = 1.96) { p <- x / n d <- 1 + z^2 / n c <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / d h <- (z / d) * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)) c(lo = pmax(0, c - h), hi = pmin(1, c + h)) } # ---- Load the tables ------------------------------------------------------- outcomes <- tbl(con, "outcomes") |> collect() dbDisconnect(con) risk <- outcomes |> filter(draft_eligible, outcome_observed_d) |> mutate( outcome_signed_udfa_d = coalesce(outcome_signed_udfa_d, FALSE), outcome_drafted_d = coalesce(outcome_drafted_d, FALSE), outcome_nfl_entry_d = coalesce(outcome_nfl_entry_d, FALSE) ) n_risk <- nrow(risk) n_players <- n_distinct(risk$playerId) # thousands-separated and percent formatters for inline numbers fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) { formatC(as.numeric(x), big.mark = ",", format = "f", digits = digits) } pct <- function(x, digits = 1) sprintf("%.*f%%", digits, 100 * x) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} *Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-10-24. Draft classes after the last complete draft are administratively right-censored and carry no outcomes, so they are excluded from every rate below rather than counted as failures.* ::: ## 1. Introduction A model that forecasts who reaches the NFL has to beat the trivial forecast that nobody does, which is right for 91.7% of draft-eligible college seasons, so this post measures that base rate and its parts, with Joe Burrow, Cam Ward, Jordan Travis, Shane Buechele, and Kyle Allen as running examples. + *Expecting the draft to be rare, under five percent of eligible seasons.* + *Expecting undrafted free-agent entry to rival the draft as an NFL route.* + *Expecting exhausted eligibility to be the most common end-of-season status.* + *Expecting the chance of NFL entry to rise over a player's eligible seasons.* + *Expecting NFL outcome prevalence to be roughly stable across draft classes.* + *Expecting most entrants to appear on an NFL roster in their entry year.* ## 2. Data ### 2.1 Every eligible season ends in exactly one of five statuses A **player-season** is one player's college season with a recorded stat line, **eligible** when the following draft comes at least three years after his high-school graduation; the table defines the five ways an eligible season can end. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} status_terms <- tribble( ~Status , ~`NFL entry` , ~Definition , "Drafted" , "Yes" , "Selected in the NFL draft held the spring after the season, reported by round: round 1, rounds 2 to 3, rounds 4 to 7." , "Signed as an undrafted free agent" , "Yes" , "Not selected in that draft, but on an NFL roster within the entry window afterward (matched by a guarded name lookup)." , "Still playing next season" , "No" , "Back on a college roster the next season; the season is one more turn of the eligibility clock, not an outcome." , "Exhausted eligibility undrafted" , "No" , "The player's last observed college season, with no draft selection and no NFL roster appearance after it." , "Left the data early" , "No" , "Absent the next season although his record says a next season should exist (a transfer with sitting time, an injury retirement, or an unobserved departure); the outcome is unknown." ) kable( status_terms, caption = "The five end-of-season statuses. NFL entry means drafted or signed as an undrafted free agent." ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: The five end-of-season statuses. NFL entry means drafted or signed as an undrafted free agent. |Status |NFL entry |Definition | |:---------------------------------|:---------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| |Drafted |Yes |Selected in the NFL draft held the spring after the season, reported by round: round 1, rounds 2 to 3, rounds 4 to 7. | |Signed as an undrafted free agent |Yes |Not selected in that draft, but on an NFL roster within the entry window afterward (matched by a guarded name lookup). | |Still playing next season |No |Back on a college roster the next season; the season is one more turn of the eligibility clock, not an outcome. | |Exhausted eligibility undrafted |No |The player's last observed college season, with no draft selection and no NFL roster appearance after it. | |Left the data early |No |Absent the next season although his record says a next season should exist (a transfer with sitting time, an injury retirement, or an unobserved departure); the outcome is unknown. | ::: ::: ### 2.2 The risk set counts seasons, while each NFL event falls on one season per player A player usually contributes several eligible seasons, so the table counts more seasons than players, and each player's NFL entry, if any, falls on exactly one of them. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} risk_set <- tibble( Measure = c("Eligible player-seasons", "Distinct players"), Count = format(c(n_risk, n_players), big.mark = ",") ) kable( risk_set, caption = "The risk set: eligible seasons with an observed outcome." ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: The risk set: eligible seasons with an observed outcome. |Measure |Count | |:-----------------------|:------| |Eligible player-seasons |68,993 | |Distinct players |36,223 | ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # The draft and UDFA events are mutually exclusive, their union is the entry # label on every row, and no player enters twice. A violation here would # poison every rate below (a naive mean(na.rm = TRUE) over a partially NA flag # once read UDFA prevalence at 35 percent instead of 4.7). ``` ::: ## 3. Results ### 3.1 Fewer than four in every hundred eligible seasons end in a draft selection ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p_drafted <- mean(risk$outcome_drafted_d) p_udfa <- mean(risk$outcome_signed_udfa_d) p_entry <- mean(risk$outcome_nfl_entry_d) n_drafted <- sum(risk$outcome_drafted_d) n_udfa <- sum(risk$outcome_signed_udfa_d) n_entry <- sum(risk$outcome_nfl_entry_d) ci_drafted <- wilson(n_drafted, n_risk) ``` ::: *Expectation: the draft is rare, under five percent of eligible seasons.* ✅ Out of every 100 eligible seasons, 3.6 end drafted and 8.3 in NFL entry by either route; the table and figures give each outcome with its 95 percent confidence interval, the range the true rate plausibly occupies (Wilson's method), and split the draft by round. ::: {.cell} entry (drafted or UDFA)" ), n_event = c( sum(risk$outcome_drafted_d), sum(risk$outcome_drafted_d & risk$outcome_draft_round_d == 1L), sum(risk$outcome_drafted_d & risk$outcome_draft_round_d %in% 2:3), Discussion ::: {.callout-important} The base rate is not fixed. - The drafted share fell by more than half across the data's span, so a model validated out of time is scored against rarer positives than it trained on. - Calibration curves and precision at fixed recall say more across years than accuracy or raw discrimination figures. ::: ::: {.callout-important} Waiting time carries signal. - The chance of entry varies about 5-fold over the eligible seasons, and the undrafted chance climbs faster than the drafted chance. - Modeling drafted status alone discards that structure, and modeling entry without routes discards the competition between them. ::: ::: {.callout-important} Entry and playing are different questions. - Nearly half of entrants play zero rookie games, so the second-stage labels (made roster, rookie games) are a separate prediction problem, not a footnote on the first. ::: Several caveats bound these figures. - The high-school graduation year is imputed for players without a recruiting record, 59.6% of eligible seasons including Burrow's and Ward's, and the imputation can mis-time redshirts and transfers, shifting rows in and out of the risk set. - The "left the data early" status is informative censoring that the pipeline flags but does not resolve. - The entry-year roster rate is partly mechanical: the undrafted link is defined by roster presence, so an undrafted entrant cannot fail it, and it reads better as a check on the link than as a finding. - Two forces plausibly drive the drafted decline and the 2016 entry jump, though neither is tested here: the stat-line population grows faster than a draft of fixed size, and NFL roster coverage deepens over the years, so the undrafted lookup catches more signings that always happened. ::: {.cell} :::

Discussion ::: {.callout-important} The base rate is not fixed. - The drafted share fell from 2.9% of the 2012 class to 1.7% of the 2026 class, so a model validated out of time is scored against rarer positives than it trained on. - Calibration curves and precision at fixed recall say more across years than accuracy or raw discrimination figures. ::: ::: {.callout-important} Waiting time carries signal. - The chance of entry varies about 6-fold over the eligible seasons, and the undrafted chance climbs faster than the drafted chance. - Modeling drafted status alone discards that structure, and modeling entry without routes discards the competition between them. ::: ::: {.callout-important} Entry and playing are different questions. - About half of entrants play zero rookie games, so the second-stage labels (made roster, rookie games) are a separate prediction problem, not a footnote on the first. ::: Several caveats bound these figures. - The high-school graduation year is imputed for players without a recruiting record, 69.8% of eligible seasons including those of Burrow and Ward, and the imputation can mis-time redshirts and transfers, shifting rows in and out of the risk set. Burrow's roster record starts the season before he enrolled, so his estimated clock starts early. - The "left the data early" status is informative censoring that the pipeline flags but does not resolve. - The entry-year roster rate is partly mechanical: the undrafted link is defined by roster presence, so an undrafted entrant cannot fail it, and it reads better as a check on the link than as a finding. - Two forces plausibly drive the drafted decline and the 2016 entry jump, though neither is tested here: the roster population grows faster than a draft of fixed size, and NFL roster coverage deepens over the years, so the undrafted lookup catches more signings that always happened.
